newsitem.title: USA: DH BLAIR PAYS $4.9 MLN TO SETTLE IPO CASE.
newsitem.headline: DH BLAIR PAYS $4.9 MLN TO SETTLE IPO CASE.

text.p: D.H. Blair & Co Inc will pay $4.9 million to settle charges that it excessively marked up the prices for sixteen initial public offerings that it underwrote between June 1993 and May 1995, according to the National Association of Securities Dealers (NASD).
D.H. Blair will pay $2 million in fines and pay nearly $2.4 million to 3,100 customers. Two company executives were fined a combined $525,000.
The firm neither admitted nor denied the allegations, NASD said.
In a statement, D.H. Blair said it consented to the settlement because of complex legal issues which could have meant a costly and lengthy legal battle "which could have taken years."

The NASD said it uncovered the overcharging after a two-year long investigation. In fourteen of the sixteen IPOs, the NASD said it found fraudulent overcharging, which is defined as mark-ups of more than ten percent.

The NASD said in two of the 16 IPOs, D.H. Blair increased the after-market price to an artificial level so its preferred customers could sell their IPO shares back to the firm, creating an artificial profit. After that, D.H. Blair used the fake price increase to solicit new investors into the stock, without disclosing the circumstances of the price increase, according to the NASD.
The NASD also said that D.H. Blair placed nearly all of the IPO shares with its own customers and "dominated and controlled" the after-market trading in all 16 securities.

Under terms of the settlement, D.H. Blair's chief executive officer Kenton Wood was fined $225,000 and suspended for 60 days and head trader Vito Capotorto was fined $300,000 and suspended for 90 days in all capacities. Both were cited for inadequate supervision, the NASD said.

The 16 securities involved were Amerigon Inc common stock, TelePad Corp units, AquaCare System units, Symbollon Corp units, Skyline Multimedia units, Linda's Flame Roasted Chicken units, Skysat Communications units; Video Update Inc units, U.S. China Industrial Exchange units, Montbatten common stock, U.S. Diagnostics Labs units, Premier Laser System units, Infosafe Systems Inc units, In-Time System units, and Sepragen Corp units.
"There is no suggestion that the affected companies knew of, or were involved in these violations," the NASD said.
"Our firm's decision to settle the NASD's complaint allows us to put this issue behind us and move ahead," D.H. Blair said.
